Queen Elizabeth I issued a royal charter on 31 December 1600 granting the East India Company exclusive trading rights for fifteen years, marking the first formal permission to trade [d3][d4]. London merchants had petitioned her for permission to sail eastward, which preceded and underpinned this grant [d1]. Later, the company secured additional trading permissions from Mughal rulers, including Jahangir in 1615 [d6] and Farooq Siyara in 1717 [d7], but these were subsequent to the initial royal charter.
